issue_request: FHIR-23706 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core Consent. It requested creating a ResearchStudyContext extension on Consent.provision as a Reference(ResearchStudy), with an invariant allowing it only for research-scoped Consents.
initial_application: Commit f42fe3d5760779e6b4967c9e2f66fcc36564eba1 added the ResearchStudyContext extension row and a Consent-level invariant to the old Consent spreadsheets, and commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 later generated a core structuredefinition-extension-consent-ResearchStudyContext.xml file when Consent source moved to generated XML.
additional_context: FHIR-31903 later eliminated Consent.scope, made Consent.category repeatable, and recorded that scope-specific guard rails belong in profiles or implementation guides. Current core source keeps Consent active but has no Consent.scope element and no core-owned consent-ResearchStudyContext StructureDefinition. Commit dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 removed R5 extension definitions from core, and the current tracked extension definition is in /home/jmandel/work/fhir-extensions/input/definitions/Consent/StructureDefinition-consent-ResearchStudyContext.xml.
reconciliation: No core source was changed. A Consent.scope-based invariant would now reference a removed element and conflict with later WG direction; the authoritative extension source is outside this core checkout and already defines the Consent.provision context and Reference(ResearchStudy) value.
